# Codemap - issue 0147, round 6: the two pinned evaluator gaps

Every file this issue has to change, one line each, with the increment it belongs to. Round 6 opens on two acceptance criteria, one per pinned scenario, and the map is a searched guess until each increment measures it.

The issue fences the scope hard: only `src/evaluator/` and its unit tests may change. Nothing under `docs/testing/` may be touched at all.

## Increment `parent-any-offer-anchor` (criterion 2, `docs/testing/at-least-parent-any-reveal`)

- `src/evaluator/offer.js` - the layer that decides which (frame, definition) pairs become an offer anchor; its descent through `selectionEntryGroup`s and `entryLink`s and its stop rules decide whether the four-level-deep `Wolf Lord` link is reached at all.
- `src/evaluator/evalTree.js` - holds tree phase 2: the offer anchor's node shape, the visibility-gate chain it carries from the groups it was descended through, and the deduplication against nodes that already hang in the frame.
- `src/evaluator/effectiveState.js` - carries base `hidden` down the gate chain and holds the effective state the asserted `isHidden` flip is read from.
- `src/evaluator/fixpoint.js` - runs the post-pass that applies modifiers to offer anchors after convergence, so a `set hidden="false"` has to reach a newly projected anchor there.
- `src/evaluator/report.js` - projects every anchor into the capability record the scenario asserts (`anchorKind`, `isHidden`, `current`).
- `src/evaluator/offer.test.js` - the unit tests of the offer set; the rule this increment establishes or supersedes is pinned here.
- `src/evaluator/offer.hiddenGate.test.js` - pins how a hidden gate above an offered definition is handled today.
- `src/evaluator/effectiveState.baseHiddenInheritance.test.js` - pins the base-hidden inheritance the gate chain relies on.

## Increment `unlimited-slot-count` (criterion 1, `docs/testing/greater-than-force-unlimited-gate`)

- `src/evaluator/constraints.js` - `evaluateLimit` deliberately produces no result for an UNLIMITED bound, and the anchor-occupancy count it does produce beside the limits exists for category anchors only, so an occupied slot whose only max limit went unlimited has no number left.
- `src/evaluator/report.js` - derives a slot's `current` from the max/min result and falls back to the category-anchor occupancy map or a literal 0; this is where the occupied slot's count is lost. Shared with the other increment.
- `src/evaluator/evaluator.js` - the facade that runs the constraints phase and the report phase and decides what the report may read; it was widened for the same occupancy map in an earlier round.
- `src/evaluator/report.test.js` - the unit tests of the `current` derivation.
- `src/evaluator/constraints.unlimitedSentinel.test.js` - pins the meaning of the written `-1` sentinel (issue 079); any change on the unlimited path is judged against it.

## Read-only, never edited

- `src/evaluator/e2e.testcatalog.test.js` - the manifest-driven runner that turns the scenarios into cases; it is the check, never an edit.
- `docs/testing/greater-than-force-unlimited-gate/` and `docs/testing/at-least-parent-any-reveal/` (`scenario.json`, `rosters/*.ros`, `README.md`) - the specification, out of scope by the issue.
- `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive/` - the frozen catalog data both scenarios are derived from.
- `docs/testing/campaign-state.json` - the campaign driver's state; it pins these two gaps and is outside the issue's fence.

## Known drift, outside this issue's fence

`docs/evaluator-architecture.md` (SS3.2 offer layer, SS4.8 `current` derivation) already went stale in earlier rounds and will go further stale with either increment. The issue's out-of-scope rule bars changing anything outside `src/evaluator/`, so it stays for the human to schedule.

increments.title: An unselected deep option appears as an offer anchor, so its reveal is observable
increments.goal: Make `docs/testing/at-least-parent-any-reveal` green: the report must carry an offer anchor for the `Wolf Lord` option in rosters where nothing in its group chain is selected, so the `set hidden="false"` gated on `atLeast 1` in the parent frame can be seen flipping at all. This is criterion 2 of the issue. It goes first because the offer layer projects every scenario's anchors: whatever widens the projection here can add or move anchors across the whole suite, and that is the risk this round has to learn early.
criteria: `npx vitest run src/evaluator` passes the cases `Szenario: at-least-parent-any-reveal > rosters/01-empty-frame-wolf-lord-hidden.ros`, `> rosters/02-one-selection-reveals-wolf-lord.ros` and `> rosters/03-two-selections-reveal-unchanged.ros`.

In those three rosters the report carries a slot with `anchorKind="offerAnchor"` for the pair defId `b8be-a71f-569c-5cdc` / targetDefId `66bc-8fc1-81a2-9cd4`, reporting `isHidden` true at the empty frame and false at one resp. two selections, `current` 0 throughout.
Rosters `04-wolf-lord-selected-self-reveal.ros` and `05-wolf-lord-twice-max-fires.ros` keep resolving the same pair as `anchorKind="occupied"` and stay green.

Nothing outside `src/evaluator/` and its unit tests changes; no file under `docs/testing/` is touched.

return.plan:
GOAL (increment `parent-any-offer-anchor`, criterion 2 of issue 0147): make `docs/testing/at-least-parent-any-reveal` rosters 01/02/03 green, keep 04/05 green, keep the whole `npx vitest run src/evaluator` run green, and change nothing outside `src/evaluator/`.

WHAT I MEASURED (throwaway node scripts against the frozen fixture, deleted again; no test run). Three separate engine defects stand between today and those three rosters. Each is reproduced below with the observation, not inferred.

DEFECT 1 - the offer descent never reaches the Wolf Lord link.
`optionDefinitionsUnder` in `src/evaluator/offer.js` (lines 127-143) descends, for a child that is an `entryLink` whose resolved target is a GROUP, into `child.resolved` only. It drops the link's OWN `children`. In the Vampire Counts catalogue the Thrall (`e37b-c827-99ac-b706`) carries `<entryLink id="2e0c-7fa1-642c-54b7" type="selectionEntryGroup" targetId="53e8-...">` and that link element declares a nested `<entryLinks><entryLink id="85fb-0691-1ee6-37f8" targetId="0719-24b8-19d4-c832"/></entryLinks>` INSIDE itself (`Vampire Counts (6th definitive edition).cat` lines 3777-3792). The chain 85fb -> group 0719 -> link 614f-c7bb-2050-c603 -> group 84fd-049b-21b4-9075 -> link b8be-a71f-569c-5cdc therefore never gets walked, and rosters 01-03 carry no capability at all for that pair (measured: 245 capabilities, 105 under the Thrall, none for b8be/66bc; roster 04 has 246 and the pair resolves `occupied`). `Catalogue.xsd` line 396 (`EntryLink` extends `SelectionEntryBase`, lines 274-287) allows `selectionEntries`/`selectionEntryGroups`/`entryLinks` under an `entryLink`, and `catalogReader.js` line 914 already reads them into `def.children` - only the descent ignores them.
FIX: when descending through a group link, walk BOTH the resolved target group's children and the link's own `children`, with the same gate chain `[...gates, child]`. Guard the two recursions with different keys in `visited` (the target group's id for the target, the link's own id for the link's children) so a shared group reached twice still lets each link contribute its local members and the recursion stays finite. Leave the `entryLink`-to-an-ENTRY branch alone: its children belong to that entry, not to the outer frame (pinned by `offer.test.js` "bietet die Option einer Option NICHT im aeusseren Rahmen an").
MEASURED BLAST RADIUS of this widening, over all three fixture corpora the repo holds: in `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive` exactly 4 owner definitions gain options - `e37b-c827-99ac-b706` (Vampire Thrall) +33, `6822-0110-a7c9-cbb0` (Vampire Count) +33, `b77b-88d5-5e80-e178` (Vampire Lord) +33, `2679-58f4-1771-662d` (Ogre Tyrant) +8 - i.e. 107 new anchor slots, 41 distinct definition ids, `b8be-a71f-569c-5cdc` among them. `src/__fixtures__/whfb6` and `scripts/__fixtures__/showcase-empire` gain nothing. Across all 81 scenarios under `docs/testing/` there are 222 `capabilities` expectations, 56 of which name no `anchorKind`/`frameDefId`/`path`; none of those 56 collides with any of the 41 added ids or their targets, so no scenario becomes ambiguous. No scenario pins a slot `path` at all, so the index shift of anchors under those 4 owners cannot break one. A new offer anchor cannot add a violation either: `constraints.js` marks every result at an offer anchor `isReportable: false` (lines 15-18, 146-157), so `firing`/`absent` expectations are untouched.

DEFECT 2 - `childId="any"` counts the frame itself, so `atLeast 1` can never fail.
A condition `atLeast 1 field=selections scope=parent childId="any"` is read with `targetChildId: null` (`catalogReader.js` line 464) and queried as `scopeKey(frameKey, null)` = "everything in this frame". `countIndex.js` `indexNodeContribution` (lines 213-264) enters every node's contribution under EVERY target of `targetsOf`, `null` included, into EVERY frame of its ancestor chain - starting with the frame that IS the node (`isImmediate === true`). A selection frame therefore counts its own `instance.count` under `null`. Measured on a synthetic catalogue with reveal modifiers gated on `atLeast N ... scope=parent childId=any`: a unit holding 0/1/2 direct selections reads 1/2/3. The scenario derives 0/1/2 (`README.md`, "Herleitung von Ist/Grenze"), and `docs/battlescribe-data-format.md` 7.6 quotes the BSData wiki - the scope entity "should sum up all field's values of DESCENDANT selections". A force node is already excluded from the `null` target for exactly this reason (`countIndex.js` lines 106-108); a selection node is not. Consequence today: `atLeast 1 parent any` holds even at an empty frame, so roster 01 would report `isHidden: false` even once the anchor exists.
FIX: in `indexNodeContribution`, at the immediate frame (`isImmediate === true`) contribute `selectionCount: 0`/`forceCount: 0` under the `null` target while keeping `costSums` intact. Keeping the costs is deliberate and load-bearing: `constraints.js` line 49 derives a percent limit's denominator with `query(ctx, limit.field, limit.scope, null, ...)`, and a percent COST limit at a selection frame must keep counting the frame's own cost. Every other target (own def id, `targetId`, `memberGroupIds`, raw `type`, effective category ids) stays exactly as it is - `scope="self"` limits that count the carrier itself must keep working.
REJECTED: subtracting `frame.instance.count` in `query.js` after the index read. Same numbers, but it duplicates knowledge of what the index holds into a second place and would need the same guard at each read site.
MEASURED BLAST RADIUS: `childId="any"` appears 92 times in the definitive corpus - 77 with `scope="roster"` (root frame; the root is no node and forces contribute 0 to `null`, so unchanged), 1 with `scope="force"` on a `limit::` field (resolved before any frame work, unchanged), and 3 with `scope="parent"`: the two `atLeast 1` conditions of this scenario (`66bc-8fc1-81a2-9cd4` and the corpus-unreachable `c791-87b9-b00a-ddb4`) and one `<repeat>` on `6eac-4ed9-4511-ff14` ("Grappling Hooks", commented `1p/model`) in the `.gst`, which no scenario and no evaluator test uses. `src/__fixtures__/whfb6/Orcs and Goblins.cat` has 25, all on a category-id scope, and no test under `src/evaluator/` builds a roster from those entries. Watch `constraints.test.js`, `limitDerivation.test.js` and `modifiers.percentCondition.test.js` for a synthetic percent-SELECTION denominator at a selection frame; if one goes red it encodes the old self-inclusive count and is to be corrected against 7.6, not worked around.

DEFECT 3 - a visibility bracket's reveal overrides the member's own written `hidden`.
`offer.js` hands each anchor the chain of groups/group-links it descended through (`gates`), `effectiveState.js` `baseHiddenOf` (lines 114-119) ORs their base `hidden` into the node's base value, and `modifiers.js` `applyModifiersOfNodes` (lines 754-771) then runs each gate's `field="hidden"` modifiers AT the node, outermost first, AFTER the node's own modifiers - last writer wins. Measured on a synthetic catalogue: a member with its own written `hidden="true"` and NO modifier at all, held by a group link with base `hidden="true"` plus a firing `set hidden="false"`, reports `isHidden: false`. It must stay hidden - the bracket became visible, the member did not. For the Wolf Lord anchor the gate chain is `[2e0c-7fa1-642c-54b7, 85fb-0691-1ee6-37f8, 614f-c7bb-2050-c603]`, and 614f carries base `hidden="true"` with a `set hidden="false"` gated on the Von Carstein bloodline, which every one of the five rosters holds. So the innermost gate would write `false` in all five and roster 01 would fail even with defects 1 and 2 fixed.
FIX: compose visibility as an OR of two independently resolved tracks instead of one shared boolean: the node's own effective hidden (own/target base value plus the node's own `hidden` modifiers) OR each gate's own effective hidden (that gate's base value plus that gate's `hidden` modifiers). A hidden bracket keeps hiding what it holds; a revealed bracket merely stops hiding and never overrules the member's own value. Mechanically this means `baseHiddenOf` no longer folds the gates' base values into the node's own base, and the gate modifiers no longer write the node's hidden slot directly - they resolve their own gate's visibility, which is then ORed into what the node reports. Pick the mechanism; the semantics above is the contract.
WHAT MUST STAY GREEN, and does under that semantics: all five cases of `offer.hiddenGate.test.js` "Sichtbarkeits-Klammer" (every member there carries no own `hidden`, so own-track = visible and the gate track decides, exactly as today, including "deckt die Option wieder auf, sobald ein Modifikator die Klammer sichtbar macht"), and both real-data blocks of the same file (the Vampire-Coast slots and Heavy/Light Armour likewise carry no own `hidden`). `effectiveState.baseHiddenInheritance.test.js` pins the base-value rule and will need its wording and possibly its assertions restated to the two-track rule - that is a unit test of the engine and is yours to correct.

ORDER OF WORK: defect 1 first (the anchor has to exist before anything about it can be observed), then 2, then 3; after each, `npx vitest run src/evaluator` tells you what moved.

DO NOT TOUCH: `evalTree.js` `selectionDefinitionsUnder` (lines 713-726) has the same link-own-children gap and feeds the mandatory phantoms and the occupied nodes' gate chains. Widening it would add mandatory phantoms and therefore VIOLATIONS across the suite, which none of this increment's criteria ask for. The occupied Wolf Lord in rosters 04/05 gets no gate chain today and passes; leave it that way. Also leave `report.js` and `fixpoint.js` alone: measured, an offer anchor already reports `current: 0`, gets its `targetDefId` and its effective name, and the post-pass already applies modifiers to it. No file under `docs/testing/` may change.

return.testPlan:
TESTS ARE NEEDED. The three E2E rosters are the specification and are already committed under `docs/testing/` - they must not be touched, and they are not enough on their own: each of the three engine rules below has to be pinned as a unit test at the layer it belongs to, so a later change that undoes one fails at that layer instead of only in a five-roster scenario.

SUITE DOC: there is NO `CLAUDE.md` under `src/evaluator/` and none under `docs/testing/` - the only ones in the repository are `./CLAUDE.md` and `./scripts/lib/CLAUDE.md`. Write the missing suite doc for the evaluator unit tests as part of your step, from what the neighbouring test files actually do, and keep it short. What those files do today, for orientation and not as a substitute for reading them: every test file is a plain vitest `describe`/`it` with German titles, installs `globalThis.DOMParser = new JSDOM().window.DOMParser` at module top, builds a MINIMAL synthetic catalogue as an XML template string in the file (real fixture catalogues are used only where the point is the real data, and then read from `src/evaluator/__fixtures__/whfb6-definitive` via `readFileSync`), drives the public facade `prepareDataset` + `evaluate` from `./evaluator.js` (or, for a layer test, `PreparedDataset.contentsOf(prepareDataset(...))` plus `buildEvalTree`/`attachOfferAnchors`), and asserts against the returned report. Nothing is mocked or stubbed anywhere in this suite.

CASES, per acceptance criterion.

CRITERION "the report carries an `offerAnchor` slot for `b8be-a71f-569c-5cdc`/`66bc-8fc1-81a2-9cd4` in rosters 01-03" -> defect 1.
File: `src/evaluator/offer.test.js`, in the existing block "Angebot unter einer belegten Auswahl: die direkten Optionen, nicht mehr". Level: unit, against a new minimal synthetic catalogue in that file (the existing `CATALOGUE_XML` has no group link with local children; extend it or add a second template beside it, as the file already does for its mandatory-option case). Command: `npx vitest run src/evaluator/offer.test.js`.
- Case 1.1: a selected unit carries an `entryLink type="selectionEntryGroup"` to a shared group, and that link element declares its own nested `<entryLinks>` with a link to a SECOND shared group whose member is an entry. Expect: the offer anchors under the unit contain the member of the second group AND the members of the linked target group. Today only the latter appears.
- Case 1.2 (depth): nest one level deeper - the locally declared group link itself carries a locally declared group link. Expect the innermost member is offered under the same unit frame. This is the shape the real data has (`2e0c` -> local `85fb` -> `0719` -> `614f` -> `84fd` -> `b8be`).
- Case 1.3 (the boundary stays): an `entryLink` whose target is an ENTRY, carrying its own nested children, is still yielded as the option and its children are NOT offered in the outer frame. This is the existing rule "die Optionen einer geschachtelten Auswahl gehoeren dieser" and must not be widened.
- Case 1.4 (repeat/cycle): two locally declared links on the same owner pointing at the SAME shared group, and a group whose local child links back to an ancestor group. Expect: the descent terminates, and no definition gets two anchors in one frame (the dedup already covers the second half - assert both, since the new `visited` keying is what makes it true).
- Case 1.5 (gates carry): make the locally declared group link `hidden="true"`. Expect the deep member's offer anchor reports `isHidden: true` - i.e. the bracket chain of the new path is the same chain the old path builds.
- Case 1.6 (empty): a group link with no local children at all behaves exactly as today (control, so the change reads as an addition).

CRITERION "`isHidden` true at the empty frame, false at one resp. two selections" -> defect 2, the counting half.
File: a new `src/evaluator/countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js` (the suite names layer tests `<module>.<topic>.test.js`; `countIndex.costSumCarrierFrame.test.js` and `countIndex.syntheticAnchors.test.js` are the nearest neighbours). Level: unit through the public facade, reading the effect off a reveal modifier or a limit rather than off the index directly. Command: `npx vitest run src/evaluator/countIndex.frameOwnAnyTarget.test.js`.
- Case 2.1: a unit whose option carries `set hidden="false"` gated on `atLeast 1 field="selections" scope="parent" childId="any"`. Roster with the unit holding NOTHING. Expect the option's slot reports `isHidden: true` (count 0). Today it reports false.
- Case 2.2: same catalogue, unit holds one direct selection. Expect `isHidden: false` (count 1).
- Case 2.3 (`atLeast` stays `atLeast`): unit holds two direct selections. Expect `isHidden: false` still.
- Case 2.4 (the exact number): three options gated on `atLeast 1`, `atLeast 2`, `atLeast 3`. With the unit holding one selection, exactly the first two are revealed - this reads the count off as 1 and would catch an off-by-one in either direction.
- Case 2.5 (nesting flag): a selection one level deeper does not count with `includeChildSelections="false"` and does count with `"true"`.
- Case 2.6 (control, own id target): a `scope="self"` limit on the frame still counts the frame itself. This is the case the fix must NOT break, and the reason it removes only the `null` target's selection count.
- Case 2.7 (control, cost): a percent limit on a COST field at a selection frame still derives its denominator including the frame's own cost. This is the second thing the fix must not break.
- Case 2.8 (control, force): `scope="force" childId="any"` is unchanged - a force frame never counted itself.

CRITERION "`isHidden` true at the empty frame" -> defect 3, the visibility half.
File: `src/evaluator/offer.hiddenGate.test.js`, beside the existing synthetic block. Level: unit through the facade, with the file's existing `catalogueWith`/`armyWithSquad`/`TOKEN_CONDITION` helpers. Command: `npx vitest run src/evaluator/offer.hiddenGate.test.js`.
- Case 3.1: a member with its OWN `hidden="true"` and no modifier, inside a shared group (or group link) that is `hidden="true"` and carries a firing `set hidden="false"`. Expect the member's offer anchor reports `isHidden: true` - the bracket became visible, the member did not. Today it reports false.
- Case 3.2 (the reveal still works): the same catalogue with the member carrying no own `hidden`. Expect `isHidden: false` once the bracket's modifier fires, `true` while it does not. This is the existing rule and its regression guard.
- Case 3.3 (own reveal wins over own base): a member with own `hidden="true"` and its own firing `set hidden="false"`, inside a visible bracket. Expect `isHidden: false`.
- Case 3.4 (bracket still hides): a member with own `hidden="false"` inside a bracket whose modifier SETS `hidden="true"`. Expect `isHidden: true`.
- Case 3.5 (cumulative): two nested brackets, the outer hidden and the inner revealed by a firing modifier. Expect `isHidden: true` - the outer still hides.
`src/evaluator/effectiveState.baseHiddenInheritance.test.js` pins the current single-track base rule; restate its wording and its assertions to the two-track rule rather than deleting it.

NOT TESTED, deliberately: the `.ros` rosters, `scenario.json` and `README.md` of `at-least-parent-any-reveal` are the specification and stay untouched - no new scenario is authored here (issue, Out of scope). The 107 extra offer anchors the widening produces in the definitive corpus are not asserted one by one; the closed check below covers them, and no expectation anywhere counts anchors. Nothing else is run. Not `npm test`, not the puppeteer E2E, not the linter, not the type check: the issue's own decision names this command, and CLAUDE.md exempts an evaluator-only change from the full run.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED, stated from reading and not from a run - I did not run the check list, not even once. In `npx vitest run src/evaluator` today, two scenarios fail: `Szenario: at-least-parent-any-reveal` rosters 01, 02 and 03 (this increment closes them; the runner fails them as a manifest error, "capabilities: kein Slot mit defId=...", because the slot does not exist at all), and `Szenario: greater-than-force-unlimited-gate` rosters 02 and 03, which belong to the OTHER increment and must stay exactly as red as they are - neither worse nor fixed here.
